extracted.intended_audience: Mathematics Stack Exchange users who want to typeset mathematical notation in posts (askers and answerers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing and editing mathematical notation on Mathematics Stack Exchange using LaTeX/MathJax, including tools, resources, and practical tips for getting formulas to render correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use LaTeX/MathJax for typesetting
rubrics_metrics.description: The equations are typeset using LaTeX; there is a link that says 'MathJax Help' when you are editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use LaTeX (rendered by MathJax) to produce math on the site; consult the MathJax Help link available while editing for site-specific tips and supported features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult the MathJax supported commands list
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a list of the LaTeX commands currently supported by MathJax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the MathJax-supported commands list to know which TeX commands will render correctly on the site; use that list when a command fails to render as expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the MathJax basic tutorial and quick reference
rubrics_metrics.description: MathJax basic tutorial and quick reference is recommended for users learning to input math here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the tutorial/quick reference to learn common MathJax usage patterns, syntax, and troubleshooting steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select inline mode when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: YEAH! You need to select 'inline' for it to work properly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some constructs require choosing the inline display mode (versus display mode) in the editor to render as intended—check the editor settings and toggle 'inline' when formulas don't behave as expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use external equation editors to build TeX
rubrics_metrics.description: You can use the CodeCogs LaTeX equation editor to form TeX expressions you can then paste into here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use online equation editors (e.g., CodeCogs, sciweavers, other editors) to build and preview LaTeX, then paste the resulting code into your post.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Detexify to find symbol names
rubrics_metrics.description: Also useful is Detexify: you draw the symbol and it performs OCR to tell you the name of the symbol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you don't know a symbol's LaTeX command, draw it in Detexify to discover the appropriate command to use in MathJax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult canonical LaTeX guides
rubrics_metrics.description: The bibles of LaTeX are the Not So Short Introduction, the Short Math Guide, and the longer amsmath guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For deeper LaTeX knowledge (syntax, environments, amsmath features), consult these established guides to write robust, well-structured mathematical markup.

rubrics_metrics.name: View source of existing posts to learn examples
rubrics_metrics.description: You can view the source of any post on the site by going to /posts/XXXXX/revisions where there is a link 'view source'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect the source of well-formatted questions/answers (via revision history or 'Show Source') to see concrete examples of LaTeX usage and copy patterns that work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right-click 'Show Source' on rendered math
rubrics_metrics.description: Without having to go to the revision history, you can look at any MathJax source by right-clicking on the math and then clicking 'Show Source'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the browser/context-menu 'Show Source' option on rendered math to quickly reveal the LaTeX (note: it omits the dollar signs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the editor's 'edit' or 'improve this question' to see source
rubrics_metrics.description: You can get to the source more directly by clicking 'edit' in the bottom left if logged in, and if a post has been edited then you can click on the time to the right of 'edited' to access the revision history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have sufficient privileges, use the post edit UI to view and learn from others' raw LaTeX source; revision timestamps link to prior versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escape characters when needed (extra backslashes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Most of the formatting is supported, though every once in a while there are a few things you need to do to get MathJax to work right (like extra \ to act as escape characters, etc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When markup doesn't render, try escaping characters (e.g., doubling backslashes) as recommended in MathJax docs or the editor help to avoid parser issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn by studying well-formatted users' posts
rubrics_metrics.description: You can learn some tricks by looking at how some of those people formatted their formulas; you probably can't do it with other people's posts yet because of your reputation, but you can do it to any posts you make if someone edits and formats them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emulate formatting techniques from high-quality posts; practice formatting on your own posts and learn from edits by others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use curated lists and sandboxes (e.g., Carol Fisher's list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Also very helpful is Carol Fisher's Alphabetical List of TEX Commands available in MathJax, which gives examples of all MathJax commands, and has a little MathJax sandbox for experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use curated command lists and sandboxes to both look up commands and to experiment safely before pasting into posts.
